name: Text from Future Me
blurb: Your phone gets texts from yourself that know exactly what happens next
title: Text from Future Me: 45-Second Sci-Fi Short Script for 1
description: A 45-second sci-fi short script for 1 actor: texts arrive from your future self, predict everything, and end on a twist. Free to film alone.
h1: Text from Future Me: a 45-Second Sci-Fi Script for 1 Actor
logline: On a lazy afternoon, Sam's phone buzzes with a message from a contact called Me. Every message comes true within seconds, and the final one changes who is really sending them.
setting: A sofa in a living room, daytime. Props: a phone, a pot of yoghurt, a sofa cushion, a TV remote.

roles.name: Sam
roles.note: Any gender, any age. Bored, curious, a little forgetful. Wants proof, then wants the upper hand.

script.action: SAM lies on the sofa, about to eat a yoghurt. The phone buzzes.

script.text: ON SCREEN: ME: Don't eat the yoghurt.

script.action: Sam checks the lid. Grimaces. Puts the yoghurt down.

script.text: ON SCREEN: ME: Your friend is about to cancel tonight.
ON SCREEN: FRIEND: So sorry, can't make it!
ON SCREEN: ME: Future you. Look under the cushion.

script.action: Sam lifts the cushion. The TV remote, missing for a week.

script.say: Fine. Future me. Tell me something big.

script.text: ON SCREEN: ME: Honestly? I'm not future you. I'm past you. I scheduled these last night. You never remember anything.

script.action: Sam opens the phone's scheduled messages. Ten more are waiting. Sam laughs.

script.say: Okay, past me. Two can play.

script.action: Sam types a message to tomorrow's self and schedules it.

script.sfx: Buzz. A new message. Not scheduled.

script.text: ON SCREEN: ME: Nice try. This one really is from the future.

script.action: Sam slowly looks from the phone to the camera.

body: Shoot vertical 9:16 on a tripod with a second phone as the prop, or film the prop phone's screen in close-up. Add every message as on-screen text in editing so viewers can read it in any language, and leave each one up for at least two seconds per line. Use natural daylight for the first half; for the last message, dim the room or turn the screen brightness up so the final shot feels colder. You only need one actor, so take three or four takes of each reaction.

ul: Every reaction gets bigger: mild confusion, then a little fear, then real shock at the remote.
React to the phone a beat after the buzz, not on it. Viewers need time to read the text.
The laugh at the scheduled messages is relief. Play it big so the last message can take it away.
The final look to camera is the whole ending. Hold it for two full seconds and do not smile.
Common mistake: reading the messages aloud. Let the screen speak; Sam only reacts.
Set it at a desk before an exam: the messages warn about a dead pen and a wrong room number.
Cast two actors: Sam on screen and Future Sam seen only as a hand typing in a dark room.
Part-two hook: Sam replies asking what happens next, and the reply is a photo of Sam's own sofa, taken from behind.

prompts.keyframe: A young adult lies on a sofa in a sunny living room holding a pot of yoghurt, looking at a glowing phone with a puzzled frown, natural daylight, shallow depth of field, cinematic still, vertical 9:16.
shots: Medium shot of a person on a sofa about to eat yoghurt, their phone buzzes, they read it, check the lid, and put the yoghurt down with a grimace, curious light comedy, daylight, vertical 9:16.
Close-up of a hand lifting a sofa cushion to reveal a lost TV remote, then tilt up to a shocked face, surprise mood, soft daylight, vertical 9:16.
Slow push-in on a person on a sofa as the phone screen glows in a dimmer room, they read a message and slowly look straight into the camera, eerie sci-fi mood, vertical 9:16.

faq.q: Do I need a second person to film this?
faq.a: No. It is written for one actor. Put the phone you film with on a tripod, use a second phone or any phone-shaped object as the prop, and add the messages as text in editing.

faq.q: Is the ending really sci-fi or just a prank?
faq.a: Both, on purpose. The scheduled messages explain everything, and then one message arrives that nobody scheduled. Leave it open, or film a part two.

faq.q: Can I use it on a monetised channel?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0, including monetised and sponsored videos. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the caption.
